framing.lineOfInquiry: Pooja Singh (P00005) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE006
framing.alternate: Pooja Singh (P00005) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: The money has a legitimate explanation
alternateHypotheses.statement: The flagged money movements of Pooja Singh have an ordinary purpose (salary, rent, property, business) or belong to a co-holder of the account.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: Flagged RTGS ₹1,250,000 on 2025-02-24 11:15 has a stated purpose 'property booking - registered sale deed' — Stated purpose 'property booking - registered sale deed' may be a legitimate explanation; verify supporting documents.

alternateHypotheses.test: Obtain full statements, invoices or agreements and KYC; confirm the stated purpose with the counter-party.

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Pooja Singh's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: In contact with Rohit Aggarwal since 2025-01-10, 29 days before the incident (13 calls, 5 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Divya Kapoor since 2025-01-10, 28 days before the incident (4 calls, 5 messages) — a long-standing relationship

alternateHypotheses.test: Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Pooja Singh was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 21 other days (09 Jan – 10 Mar), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Pooja Singh was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded in the FIR as complainant, not as accused

alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was elsewhere at the time (alibi)
alternateHypotheses.statement: Pooja Singh was somewhere else when the incident happened.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded at an unnamed place, 16.7 km from the scene, 73 min after the incident — the scene was reachable by road in that time, so this is only a partial alibi

alternateHypotheses.test: Verify the alibi record independently (CCTV, witnesses or receipts at that place and time) and check whether the device could have been carried by someone else.

alternateHypotheses.title: Mistaken identity
alternateHypotheses.statement: Records belonging to someone else (a namesake or a wrongly matched profile) were attributed to Pooja Singh.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: 1 other person record(s) share the name 'Pooja Singh' (P00006), so name-based records can be misattributed

alternateHypotheses.test: Confirm identity with photograph or fingerprints (NAFIS), father's name and address from the FIR particulars.

alternatesConsideredNotSupported.title: Someone else used the phone or handset

comparison.verdict: Every supporting item could be explained by at least one alternate, although the line of inquiry is stronger on weight (0.73 vs 0.44). Test the alternates before relying on it.
settleWith: A4 — Obtain full statements, invoices or agreements and KYC; confirm the stated purpose with the counter-party.
A5 — Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.
A2 — Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).
